QUOTE: Without `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS`, `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member)` expands to `private_##member`. With it defined, the macro expands to `member`. ... `library/common.h:132` defines `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` globally. Every `library/*.c` file includes `common.h` ... so the library sees the real field names.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says the two macro branches give different spellings. Code that defines the opt-out (the library, programs, tests) sees real names, and an ordinary consumer sees the `private_`-mangled names.
